body.statement: Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and a positive certificate. Use \(\operatorname{vec}_H=(\iota_C,\iota_Y)\), the \(k_Y\times m_H\) Jacobian \(J_H\), \(\operatorname{IF}_H(c)=J_H(\mathbf p_H)(e_c^C-\mathbf p_H)\), and \(\Sigma_H=\operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\operatorname{IF}_H(V,S)\}\). At every fixed \(p_H\) in the differentiable interior of its branch-specific \(\mathfrak D_H\), \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\), and \(F_H(\widehat p_H)\) is asymptotically linear on the on-domain event. For fixed \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), set \(\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}F_H(\widehat p_H)\), \(\widehat v_{H,y}=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_H e_y^Y\), and \(CI_y=[\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}/n}]\). If \(\Sigma_H\{\iota_Y(y),\iota_Y(y)\}>0\), then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.\] For fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), use the defined \(CI_{\lambda}\); then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_{\lambda}\}=1-\alpha.\] Thus the coverage targets are respectively the single component \(Q_{a,H}(y)\) and the fixed scalar contrast \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\), each pointwise at the fixed interior law. On the off-domain event the procedure returns \(\bot_H\) and no confidence set; no positivity-boundary-uniform coverage is claimed.
body.justification: The statistical rung turns every positive graphical certificate into an estimable finite-table causal functional.
body.gap: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive inference for fixing functionals, but not for one joint fixed-support selector table generated by the proposed complete calculus.
body.consumer: Applied users of a selector-aware dosearch backend obtain point estimates, standard errors, and pointwise Wald intervals from the same returned circuit.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\) be fixed in the stated differentiable interior.  Because \(\mathfrak D_H\) is defined by finitely many strict inequalities in continuous polynomials, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(N\) of \(\mathbf p_H\) contained in \(\mathfrak D_H\).  For every cell \(c\),
\[
E\{\widehat p_H(c)\}=p_H(c),
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}\{\widehat p_H(c)\}=\frac{p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}}{n}.
\]
For every \(\delta>0\), the pointwise inequality \(\delta^2\mathbf 1\{|\widehat p_H(c)-p_H(c)|\ge\delta\}\le\{\widehat p_H(c)-p_H(c)\}^2\), followed by expectation and a union bound over the finite cell set, gives \(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\to\mathbf p_H\) in probability.  Hence
\[
\Pr\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}
\le \Pr\{\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\notin N\}\longrightarrow0. \tag{10}
\]

On \(N\), the registered denominators are positive, so the rational circuit has a continuously differentiable ambient extension.  First-order differentiability gives
\[
F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)
=J_H(\mathbf p_H)(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)
+o_p(n^{-1/2}). \tag{11}
\]
The equality
\[
J_H(\mathbf p_H)(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
J_H(\mathbf p_H)(e_{(V_i,S_i)}^C-\mathbf p_H)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{IF}_H(V_i,S_i) \tag{12}
\]
identifies the influence function and proves the asserted asymptotic linearity on the on-domain event.  The remainder in (11) is \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\) because \(\sqrt n(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)=O_p(1)\) in the finite multinomial model.  The smooth empirical plug-in is regular under local interior multinomial perturbations, since the same derivative in (11) applies along every such perturbation.  Applying \(\textnormal{lem:asymptotic-linear-normality}\) to a fixed vector \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_Y}\) and the scalar influence function \(c^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{IF}_H\) yields
\[
\sqrt n\,c^{\mathsf T}\{F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)\}
\ \rightsquigarrow\ N(0,c^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Hc). \tag{13}
\]

The map
\[
(q,J)\longmapsto
\sum_c q(c)J(e_c^C-q)(e_c^C-q)^{\mathsf T}J^{\mathsf T}
\]
is continuous at \((\mathbf p_H,J_H(\mathbf p_H))\), and \(J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)\to J_H(\mathbf p_H)\) in probability.  Therefore
\[
\widehat\Sigma_H\longrightarrow\Sigma_H \quad\text{in probability}. \tag{14}
\]
Certificate soundness gives \(F_H(p_H)=Q_{a,H}\).  If the component variance \(v_{H,y}=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H e_y^Y\) is positive, take \(c=e_y^Y\) in (13).  Equation (14) gives \(\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}\to1\) in probability.  For any \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), the event \(|\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}-1|\le\varepsilon\) squeezes the studentized statistic between the corresponding fixed rescalings of the statistic in (13).  The limiting normal distribution has a continuous distribution function; letting first \(n\to\infty\) and then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and using the definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\), gives
\[
\Pr\{Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\mid \widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Together with (10), this is equivalent to the displayed joint-event limit in the proposition.  Replacing \(e_y^Y\) by a fixed \(\lambda\ne0\) gives the second limit whenever \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\).  Off the event in (10), the definition returns \(\bot_H\) and constructs no interval, so no boundary or off-domain coverage statement has been used.
